requirement.description: The HTTP/2 hook implementation creates records but does not properly populate them with request/response data. The hooks only create placeholders and don't capture actual HTTP/2 data flow from the underlying HTTP/2 connection.
requirement.contract: The HTTP/2 hooks must properly capture HTTP/2 request and response data including: - URL construction from HTTP/2 pseudo-headers (:authority, :path) - Method extraction from :method pseudo-header - Status code extraction from :status pseudo-header - Headers parsing from HTTP/2 frames - Content body extraction from HTTP/2 frames - Cookies from headers - Protocol identification as "HTTP/2" - Proper exception handling with correct exception type and message

requirement.description: The HTTP/2 record implementation does not properly capture and store HTTP/2 frame data. It only implements basic property getters but doesn't integrate with the actual HTTP/2 connection to capture real data flows.
requirement.contract: The HTTP/2 record class must: - Receive and store HTTP/2 frame data via send_data() and receive_data() methods - Properly parse HTTP/2 pseudo-headers for URL, method, status, etc. - Extract and store content from HTTP/2 data frames - Maintain accurate timestamps for last updates - Support proper URL construction from HTTP/2 pseudo-headers - Ensure headers are properly formatted for HTTP/2

requirement.description: The HTTP/2 hook implementation does not correctly integrate with the HTTP/2 connection mechanism. It creates records but doesn't hook into the actual HTTP/2 transport layer to capture the data flow.
requirement.contract: The HTTP/2 hook implementation must: - Properly hook into HTTP/2 connections at the transport layer - Integrate with HTTP/2 frame processing to capture request/response data - Ensure that HTTP/2 connection handlers can update records with actual data - Support both synchronous and asynchronous HTTP/2 clients - Handle HTTP/2 specific connection events like stream creation and termination

requirement.description: The records system doesn't properly distinguish between HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 records during creation, causing HTTP/2 records to be created as HTTP/1 records.
requirement.contract: The HTTPRecords.add_new_record method must: - Accept a record_type parameter to differentiate between HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 records - Create appropriate record instances based on the record_type parameter - Ensure HTTP/2 records are instantiated with the correct HTTP2Record class

requirement.description: The HTTP/2 hook implementation is incomplete - it doesn't capture the actual HTTP/2 frame data that would be needed to populate the record properties.
requirement.contract: The HTTP/2 hook implementation must: - Hook into the actual HTTP/2 connection mechanism (not just method decoration) - Ensure that HTTP/2 data frames are properly captured and passed to the records - Support HTTP/2 stream management for proper request/response correlation - Handle both client and server-side HTTP/2 interactions
